title: Relative ampleness can be checked on an affine open cover of the base
statement: Let $h:Z\to S$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and let $N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose $S=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ is an affine open covering and $N|_{h^{-1}(U_i)}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] for every $i\in I$. Then $N|_{h^{-1}(V)}$ is ample for every affine open $V\subseteq S$.

source.place: Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), implication (3) implies (1). The conclusion unfolds f-ampleness into ampleness over every affine open of the base.

proof.text: Put $Z_i=h^{-1}(U_i)$, $h_i:Z_i\to U_i$, and $N_i=N|_{Z_i}$. For an arbitrary affine open $W\subseteq U_i$, the inclusion $W\to U_i$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. Its base change $a:h_i^{-1}(W)\to Z_i$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1). Here $Z_i\times_{U_i}W=h_i^{-1}(W)$: a map into either side is a map into $Z_i$ whose composite to $U_i$ factors through the open $W$. The pullback $a^*N_i$ is its restriction, since the formula in [def-pc-module-pullback] reduces on an open immersion to $\mathcal O\otimes_{\mathcal O}N_i|=N_i|$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible], this restriction is ample. Moreover $h_i$ is quasi-compact: each affine open $W\subseteq U_i$ is an affine open of $S$, and $h_i^{-1}(W)=h^{-1}(W)$ is quasi-compact by the given quasi-compactness of $h$. These two facts together give $h_i$-ampleness of $N_i$ in the current, quasi-compactness-inclusive sense of [lem-trf-scheme-ample-canonical-proj-criterion].

source.place: Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), (3) implies (5), with the affine-base reduction justified by the affine specialization of Tag 0892 (lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample)(2).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-scheme-ample-canonical-proj-criterion] to the quasi-compact $(h_i,N_i)$ of Step 1. Its forward implication gives quasi-separatedness of $h_i$, the canonical section algebra $\mathcal A_i=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}(h_i)_*N_i^{\otimes d}$ with evaluation $\psi_i$, the equality $U(\psi_i)=Z_i$, and an open immersion $r_i:Z_i\to\operatorname{Proj}_{U_i}(\mathcal A_i)$. Its final assertion also makes $h_i$ separated. Thus the criterion is applied with its quasi-compactness hypothesis already established; its algebra is formed only after obtaining quasi-separatedness.

source.place: Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), local canonical section-algebra maps in the proof of (3) implies (5); Tag 01VI (lemma-relatively-ample-separated).

proof.text: View our schemes as representable algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Check the local $h_i$ against the definitions in [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]. For each affine scheme $T\to U_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3) makes $q:Z_i\times_{U_i}T\to T$ quasi-compact. Its identity presentation is the required surjective etale presentation by a quasi-compact scheme. Hence $h_i$ is quasi-compact as a space morphism. Its scheme diagonal is a closed immersion by Step 2 and [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Every scheme test of the representable diagonal is a base change of this same scheme diagonal (both fibre products classify pairs with equal image). It is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Thus $h_i$ is separated as a space morphism as well.

source.place: Tags 03KG (lemma-quasi-compact-local), 03KM (lemma-separated-local), scheme tests; schemes.tex Tag 01K5 (lemma-quasi-compact-preserved-base-change); morphisms.tex Tag 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion).

proof.text: The inclusions $U_i\hookrightarrow S$ are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1) and jointly surjective by hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local] to $h$ and this family, whose base changes are the $h_i$ checked in Step 3. It gives quasi-compactness and separatedness in the space sense. To recover scheme separatedness, take the scheme test $Z\times_SZ\to Z\times_SZ$ equal to the identity in its representable diagonal: the resulting closed immersion is exactly $\Delta_h:Z\to Z\times_SZ$. Thus $h$ is scheme-separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; its scheme quasi-compactness is the original hypothesis. Moreover [def-weil-closed-immersion] says $\Delta_h$ is affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) makes it quasi-compact. Consequently $h$ is quasi-separated by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], as required for the current canonical-Proj criterion.

source.place: Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), first paragraph of (3) implies (5); spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03KG, 03KM; schemes.tex Tag 01KK (definition-separated), and Tag 01K6 (lemma-closed-immersion-quasi-compact).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], $N$ corresponds to a line module on the small etale site of $Z$, and its direct images and pullbacks agree with the Zariski ones under that equivalence. Use [lem-trf-space-section-algebra-etale-base-change] for the quasi-compact separated $h$ from Step 4. It supplies the quasi-coherent graded algebra $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}h_*N^{\otimes d}$ on $S$ and its evaluation map $\psi:h^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{d\geq0}N^{\otimes d}$. For each $U_i\to S$, it identifies $\mathcal A|_{U_i}$ with $\mathcal A_i$ and the restricted evaluation with $\psi_i$. Its last clause identifies all these maps with the ordinary scheme maps, so the canonical criterion of Step 2 concerns exactly these algebras and evaluations.

source.place: Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), section-algebra and adjunction paragraphs; descent.tex Tags 03DX,03LC and spaces-properties.tex Tag 03LX for the existing comparison interfaces.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map] to $(h,N,\mathcal A,\psi)$. It gives an open $U(\psi)\subseteq Z$ and a canonical map $r:U(\psi)\to P=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal A)$. Its restriction compatibility and Step 5 identify $U(\psi)\cap Z_i$ with $U(\psi_i)=Z_i$, and identify the restricted map with $r_i$ under $P\times_SU_i\simeq\operatorname{Proj}_{U_i}(\mathcal A_i)$. Since the $Z_i$ cover $Z$, the first equality gives $U(\psi)=Z$: every point belongs to a $Z_i$ and hence to $U(\psi)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] applied to the covering family of Step 4 and $P\to S$, the schemes $P\times_SU_i$ form a jointly surjective etale family over $P$. The base changes of $r:Z\to P$ to this family are exactly the open immersions $r_i$ of Step 2. Thus [lem-trf-space-open-immersion-etale-local] implies that $r$ is an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), conclusion of (3) implies (5); constructions.tex Tag 01O9, spaces-divisors.tex Tag 0D2Z for restriction compatibility.

proof.text: The original hypothesis makes $h$ quasi-compact, and Step 4 proves it quasi-separated. Steps 5 and 6 give its canonical graded algebra and evaluation with full generation locus $Z$ and canonical Proj map an open immersion. Thus condition (2) of [lem-trf-scheme-ample-canonical-proj-criterion] holds, with all its prerequisites. Its reverse implication gives $h$-ampleness of $N$, which the statement defines to include precisely ampleness of $N|_{h^{-1}(V)}$ for every affine open $V\subseteq S$. This is the required conclusion.
